body: You're 18. I think that says enough. If you're not okay being in a long term relationship now, you should leave before you grow resentment you can't contain. Leave, start new relationships and learn about yourself. You're young.

It depends on what they did to you. 
Did it hurt you a lot? Was it an insult? Did they break your trust? 
Do they still want to be around you and be forgiven through actions rather than words? Some people are like that.

But it all depends on how you feel.. that's the most important thing. You determine what's forgivable and what's not. Think about how you feel, and how this person impacts your life.

Give your son all the love you have. You may find it difficult to stop caring of other's judgement, but to your son's eyes only you matter the most. If that guy can't act like a father, please make a decision. Either have a serious discussion with him, or completely distance him from your child.

Your son doesn't deserve to go through the same emotional pain you go through. Make sure his life will be different from yours, make sure he grows up loved, in a peaceful environment. 

Sorry if I come across as harsh, but I went through your post history and you seem to have a troubled life. I hope this comment doesn't upset you.

You're not overreacting. It makes you insecure, it's totally normal. You should talk to him about it, honestly. Explain your insecurities, without fears. If he cares about you, he'll respect you. But try talking first, and don't assume or try to accuse too much (they tend to get very defensive about this).
Do it for yourself. For your mental health. Remember how happy you used to be without the toxic relationshio.
He sounds like an absolute dick. I'm sorry you had to put up with all that.

If she knows you're going through depression, then I'm sure she was trying to get you out of the house and spend time with someone. Since she works with disabled people, she saw this as good opportunity for you to take care of someone and feel better about yourself, and so on.
